brief:
Several European countries are maintaining military cooperation and weapons agreements with Israel as the conflict in Gaza persists, Shehab Wire reported. The continued arms transfers and new military contracts have provoked sharp criticism from rights groups and international observers who warn that supplying weapons during active hostilities may expose these nations to legal liability.

The controversy centers on whether European governments should proceed with defense sales and military cooperation agreements at a time when Gaza faces sustained military operations. Critics contend that providing weaponry or signing new military deals during the conflict raises serious questions about potential complicity in violations of international humanitarian law.
